description.narrative: The SHARP project (Taadoud) is multi-year initiative funded by DFID in Sudan. The implementing members of the partnership are a group of 6 INGOs (CAFOD, Oxfam, World Vision, NCA, CRS, and UMCOR) together with Tufts University. Each member of the partnership brings in special skills and comparative advantage in order to enhance livelihood resilience in Darfur. CAFOD takes the role of leading in building capacity of the NGOs and partners in delivery of Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) among the NGOs, partners and community based organisations (CBOs). The implementation strategy is designed to maximize partnership members’ strengths and comparative advantages; to build capacity of national partners and government within their current work; to mitigate risks; and to promote sustainability. The strategic design is rooted in a strong emphasis and investment in human and social assets. Through this design, Taadoud will promote the sustainable transfer of skills and knowledge which will outlast the value of supplies and materials. It is anticipated that the new skills and knowledge will be housed in local communities to be used as a resource for future generations. Focusing on human and social assets will have a multiplier effect so that the other asset categories will benefit including political, financial, natural and physical assets by the improvement of local decision-making coordination and management. The logic of this intervention underpins the role of communities and households in all activities so that they are involved from the inception to influence the project so that their resilience is strengthened. At the consortium level, different members offers technical lead on activities for which they have successful experience in Sudan and globally. CAFOD leads in; CB-DRR and CB-EW, CAFOD has available trainers, tools and guidance, CRS leads; in SILC, CGM, homestead gardens and EMMA, while NCA leads Agricultural extension, Oxfam offers technical lead in Micro-insurance pilot and UMCOR in Peace-building integration finally WV offers technical lead in Pastoral extension and CAHWs. The project has received two extension; one is no cost extension which ends in September 2016 and a cost extension which runs up to August, 2017.
